```{r}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Load and clean ELA data (5-year cohort window)
YEAR <- 2025

# Dynamically construct raw GitHub URLs for ELA database
csv_url1 <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reading4All/NY/refs/heads/main/data/ELA/DATA_ELA-SPRING-", YEAR, ".csv")
csv_url2 <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reading4All/NY/refs/heads/main/data/ELA/DATA_ELA-SPRING-", YEAR-1, ".csv")
csv_url3 <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reading4All/NY/refs/heads/main/data/ELA/DATA_ELA-SPRING-", YEAR-2, ".csv")
csv_url4 <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reading4All/NY/refs/heads/main/data/ELA/DATA_ELA-SPRING-", YEAR-3, ".csv")
csv_url5 <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reading4All/NY/refs/heads/main/data/ELA/DATA_ELA-SPRING-", YEAR-4, ".csv")

# Safely read and combine raw ELA files from GitHub
read_safe_csv <- function(url) {
  tryCatch({
    read_csv(url, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Fail-safe empty dataframe with expected columns if URL fails
    data.frame(
      ENTITY_CD = character(), ENTITY_NAME = character(), YEAR = character(), 
      ASSESSMENT_NAME = character(), SUBGROUP_NAME = character(), 
      Prof_Count = character(), NotProf_Count = character(), NOT_TESTED = character(),
      Prof_Pct = character(), NotProf_Pct = character(), PER_PROF = character(),
      SEASON = character(), ENTITY_TYPE = character(), COUNTY_DESC = character()
    )
  })
}

df1 <- read_safe_csv(csv_url1)
df2 <- read_safe_csv(csv_url2)
df3 <- read_safe_csv(csv_url3)
df4 <- read_safe_csv(csv_url4)
df5 <- read_safe_csv(csv_url5)

ela_data <- rbind(df1, df2, df3, df4, df5)

# Keep only Spring (year-end) district/county data, strictly filtered to "Students with Disabilities"
ela_clean <- ela_data %>%
  filter(
    SEASON == "Spring",
    ENTITY_TYPE %in% c("DISTRICT", "COUNTY"),
    SUBGROUP_NAME == "Students with Disabilities",
    !is.na(Prof_Pct)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    YEAR = as.numeric(YEAR),
    Prof_Count = as.numeric(Prof_Count),
    NotProf_Count = as.numeric(NotProf_Count),
    NOT_TESTED = as.numeric(NOT_TESTED),
    Prof_Pct = as.numeric(Prof_Pct),
    NotProf_Pct = as.numeric(NotProf_Pct),
    PER_PROF = as.numeric(PER_PROF)
  ) %>%
  # Strip out NYC districts to match DistrictELAGrowth layout size constraints
  filter(!startsWith(tolower(ENTITY_NAME), "nyc geo")) %>%
  select(ENTITY_NAME, COUNTY_DESC, YEAR, ASSESSMENT_NAME, SUBGROUP_NAME, Prof_Count, NotProf_Count, NOT_TESTED, Prof_Pct, NotProf_Pct, PER_PROF)

# 2. Load and Clean raw Spending Text database from GitHub
spending_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reading4All/NY/refs/heads/main/data/SPENDING%2CENROLLMENT/slfs_essa_financial_merged_thru2025.txt"

# Safe read checking tab or space delimiters dynamically
spending_raw <- tryCatch({
  df <- read_delim(spending_url, delim = "\t", col_names = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
  if (ncol(df) < 5) stop("Not tab delimited")
  df
}, error = function(e) {
  read_delim(spending_url, delim = " ", col_names = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
})

# Explicitly assign standard headers to prevent index shifting
colnames(spending_raw) <- c(
  "ENTITY_CD", "ENTITY_NAME", "YEAR", "PK12_Enrollment", "SWD_Enrollment", 
  "Special_Education_Expenditures", "Special_Education_Expenditures_PerSWD", 
  "Total_Expenditures", "Total_Instructional_Expenditures", 
  "Total_Expenditures_PerPupil", "Special_Education_Expenditures_PerPupil"
)

spending_clean <- spending_raw %>%
  mutate(
    YEAR = as.numeric(YEAR),
    PK12_Enrollment = as.numeric(PK12_Enrollment),
    SWD_Enrollment = as.numeric(SWD_Enrollment),
    Special_Education_Expenditures = as.numeric(Special_Education_Expenditures),
    Special_Education_Expenditures_PerPupil = as.numeric(Special_Education_Expenditures_PerPupil)
  ) %>%
  select(ENTITY_NAME, YEAR, PK12_Enrollment, SWD_Enrollment, Special_Education_Expenditures, Special_Education_Expenditures_PerPupil)

# Pass ELA and Spending databases separately to Observable JS
ojs_define(
  ela_to_js = ela_clean,
  spending_to_js = spending_clean
)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// 1. Transpose the separate ELA and Spending dataframes in OJS
shared_ela = transpose(ela_to_js)
shared_spending = transpose(spending_to_js)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// 2. Identify unique counties and dynamically calculate matching districts (from ELA data)
uniqueCounties = new Set(shared_ela.map(d => d.COUNTY_DESC).filter(Boolean));

districtsInCounty = new Set(
  shared_ela
    .filter(d => d.COUNTY_DESC && d.COUNTY_DESC.toUpperCase() === county.toUpperCase())
    .map(d => d.ENTITY_NAME)
);

districtDefault = {
  county;
  return "";
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// 3. Submit/Reset guard function exactly matching DistrictELAGrowth.qmd architecture
function guard(fn, options = {}, countyView) {
  const {
    submitLabel = "Submit",
    resetLabel = "Reset",
    required = false,
    resubmit = true,
    width = "100%",
    justify = "start"
  } = options;
  const onSubmit = () => {
    value = input.value;
    submit.disabled = !resubmit || invalid;
    reset.disabled = true;
    wrapper.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  };
  const onReset = () => {
    input.value = value;
    submit.disabled = !resubmit || invalid;
    reset.disabled = true;
  };
  const onInnerInputCapture = () => {
    invalid = true;
    submit.disabled = true;
  };
  const onInnerInput = e => {
    e.stopPropagation();
    submit.disabled = false;
    reset.disabled = false;
  };
  const submit = htl.html`<button ${ { disabled: !resubmit && !required, onclick: onSubmit } } class="btn btn-primary btn-sm">${submitLabel}</button>`;
  const reset = htl.html`<button ${ { disabled: true, onclick: onReset } } class=\"btn btn-secondary btn-sm\">${resetLabel}</button>`;
  const footer = htl.html`
    <div>
      <hr style="padding:0;margin:10px 0">
      <div style="display:flex;gap:1ch;justify-content: ${justify} ">
        ${submit}
      </div>
    </div>
  `;
  const template = inputs => {
    const row = document.createElement("div");
    row.className = "input-toolbar";
    row.append(countyView);
    (Array.isArray(inputs) ? inputs : Object.values(inputs))
      .forEach(input => row.append(input));
    const container = document.createElement("div");
    container.style.cssText = "width:100%;max-width:100%;min-width:0;box-sizing:border-box";
    container.append(row, footer);
    return container;
  };
  const input = fn({ submit, reset, footer, template, onSubmit, onReset });
  let invalid = !!input.querySelector(":invalid");
  submit.disabled = !resubmit || invalid;
  input.addEventListener("input", onInnerInputCapture, { capture: true });
  input.addEventListener("input", onInnerInput);
  let value = required ? undefined : input.value;
  const wrapper = htl.html`<div style="width: ${width} ">${input}`;
  wrapper.addEventListener("submit", onSubmit);
  return Object.defineProperty(wrapper, "value", {
    get: () => value,
    set: v => { input.value = v }
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
// Woven Inputs Form for District and Target Grade (Subgroup removed as it is locked to Students with Disabilities)
viewof inputSels = guard(
  ({ template }) => Inputs.form(
    {
      district: Inputs.select(districtsInCounty, {
        value: districtDefault,
        label: "District: ",
        sort: true,
        required: true
      }),
      grade: Inputs.select(
        new Map([
          ["Grade 5", 5],
          ["Grade 6", 6],
          ["Grade 7", 7],
          ["Grade 8", 8]
        ]),
        {
          value: 8,
          label: "Ending Grade (in May 2025): ",
          sort: true,
          required: true
        }
      )
    },
    { template }
  ),
  {
    resetLabel: "Reset",
    required: true,
    width: "100%"
  },
  viewof county
);
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
baseYear = 2025

// Build a dynamic year-to-year cohort sequence tracking the SAME kids back to Grade 3
gradeSequence = {
  if (!inputSels) return [];
  const g = inputSels.grade;
  return [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    .filter(offset => (g - offset) >= 3)
    .map(offset => ({
      year: baseYear - offset,
      assessment: `ELA${g - offset}`
    }));
}

// Filter ELA dataset strictly to selected District and Cohort Grades
shared_elaFiltered = {
  if (!inputSels) return [];
  const district = inputSels.district.trim().toUpperCase();
  return shared_ela.filter(d => 
    d.ENTITY_NAME.toUpperCase() === district &&
    gradeSequence.some(g => Number(g.year) === Number(d.YEAR) && g.assessment === d.ASSESSMENT_NAME)
  );
}

// Filter Spending dataset strictly to selected District
shared_spendingFiltered = {
  if (!inputSels) return [];
  const district = inputSels.district.trim().toUpperCase();
  return shared_spending.filter(d => 
    d.ENTITY_NAME.toUpperCase() === district
  );
}

// Human-friendly grade labels for x-axis
gradeLabel = assessment => `Grade ${assessment.replace("ELA", "")}`
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Calculate Cumulative Spending year-by-year as this specific cohort moves through school
cumulativeSpendData = {
  if (!inputSels || shared_spendingFiltered.length === 0) return [];
  
  // Sort years from earliest (e.g. 2020) to latest (e.g. 2025)
  const sortedYears = [...gradeSequence].sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year);
  
  let cumulativeSum = 0;
  return sortedYears.map(g => {
    // Locate the row matching this year in the district's spending data
    const row = shared_spendingFiltered.find(d => Number(d.YEAR) === Number(g.year));
    const annualSpend = (row && row.Special_Education_Expenditures_PerPupil) ? +row.Special_Education_Expenditures_PerPupil : 0;
    cumulativeSum += annualSpend;
    
    return {
      year: g.year,
      label: `${g.year}\\n${gradeLabel(g.assessment)}`,
      annualSpend: annualSpend,
      cumulativeSpend: cumulativeSum
    };
  });
}

// Format the cohort ELA percentages strictly based on full cohort size to bypass opt-out bias
subgroupCohortData = {
  if (!inputSels || shared_elaFiltered.length === 0) return [];
  
  const subgroupName = "Students with Disabilities";
  const sortedYears = [...gradeSequence].sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year);
  
  const byYear = sortedYears.map(({ year, assessment }) => {
    const row = shared_elaFiltered.find(d => 
      Number(d.YEAR) === Number(year) && 
      d.ASSESSMENT_NAME === assessment && 
      d.SUBGROUP_NAME === subgroupName
    );
    
    const prof = row ? +row.Prof_Count : 0;
    const notProf = row ? +row.NotProf_Count : 0;
    const notTested = row ? +row.NOT_TESTED : 0;
    const total = prof + notProf + notTested;
    
    return {
      YEAR: year,
      label: `${year}\\n${gradeLabel(assessment)}`,
      profPct: total > 0 ? (prof / total) * 100 : 0,
      notProfPct: total > 0 ? (notProf / total) * 100 : 0,
      notTestedPct: total > 0 ? (notTested / total) * 100 : 0,
      profCount: prof,
      notProfCount: notProf,
      notTestedCount: notTested
    };
  });
  
  // Flatten into stacked structure for Observable Plot
  return byYear.flatMap(d => [
    { label: d.label, category: "Proficient", percent: d.profPct, count: d.profCount },
    { label: d.label, category: "Not Proficient", percent: d.notProfPct, count: d.notProfCount },
    { label: d.label, category: "Not Tested", percent: d.notTestedPct, count: d.notTestedCount }
  ]);
}
```

## Plots - side by side
### PLOT A - Spending
```{ojs}
// Render the rising curve of cumulative special education per-pupil spending standard
Plot.plot({
  width: 600,
  height: 400,
  marginLeft: 80,
  marginBottom: 50,
  title: "Special Ed Spending",
  y: {
    label: "SPED $ Spent (cumulative)",
    grid: true,
    labelAnchor: "center"
  },
  x: {
    label: null,
    domain: cumulativeSpendData.map(d => d.label)
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.line(cumulativeSpendData, { x: "label", y: "cumulativeSpend", stroke: "#122C4F", strokeWidth: 3 }),
    Plot.dot(cumulativeSpendData, { x: "label", y: "cumulativeSpend", fill: "#3DAE44", r: 6, stroke: "#122C4F", strokeWidth: 1.5, tip: true }),
    Plot.text(cumulativeSpendData, {
      x: "label",
      y: "cumulativeSpend",
      text: d => `$${Math.round(d.cumulativeSpend).toLocaleString()}`,
      dy: -15,
      fontSize: 10,
      fontWeight: "bold",
      fill: "#122C4F"
    })
  ]
})
```

### PLOT B - ELA Growth
```{ojs}
// Render the stacked ELA cohort outcomes based on full cohort to eliminate opt-out distortions
Plot.plot({
  width: 600,
  height: 400,
  marginLeft: 80,
  marginBottom: 50,
  title: "Students with Disabilities - ELA Scores",
  y: {
    label: "% of Enrolled Cohort Students",
    grid: true,
    labelAnchor: "center",
    domain: [0, 100]
  },
  x: {
    label: null,
    domain: gradeSequence.sort((a,b) => a.year - b.year).map(g => `${g.year}\\n${gradeLabel(g.assessment)}`)
  },
  color: {
    domain: ["Proficient", "Not Proficient", "Not Tested"],
    range: ["#2F7F73", "#D95C5C", "#B7BDC4"],
    legend: true
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY([0]),
    Plot.barY(subgroupCohortData, Plot.stackY({
      x: "label",
      y: "percent",
      fill: "category",
      tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.category}:\n${d.count} Students\n(${d.percent.toFixed(1)}% of entire cohort)`
    }))
  ]
})
```
<!-- ## Notes: -->

<!-- Why This Page Exposes the Reading Bottleneck: -->
<!-- 1. **The Cumulative \"Mountain of Cash\" Standard (All Grades combined):** Plot A calculates the distributed special education footprint per pupil under our *Total Enrollment Standard* (`Special_Education_Expenditures_PerPupil`). Special Education budgets in New York are reported district-wide for all grade levels (PK-12) combined, rather than on a grade-specific basis. This plot sums up the overall special education budget allocation per total student over the course of the cohort's school career. By the end of Grade 8, parents can see if a district has spent **$15,000 to $20,000+ per student** purely on the footprint of special education instruction. -->
<!-- 2. **The Truth About \"Averages\" (Opt-Out Bypass):** Plot B stacks **Proficient** (Green), **Not Proficient** (Red), and **Not Tested / Opted Out** (Gray) relative to the *entire enrolled cohort* of Students with Disabilities. If a wealthy district claims a \"90% proficiency rate\" but has an expanding gray band of opted-out students while the green band narrows, it visually shatters the illusion.  -->
<!-- 3. **The Divergence Paradox:** By placing these plots side-by-side, parents can ask the central question of accountability: *“If the taxpayer bill in Plot A is climbing steeply year-over-year, why are reading proficiencies in Plot B flatlining or shrinking as our children grow older? This is not a resource crisis—this is a curriculum crisis.”* -->
